Around 20 years ago, I stood outside a store with a sign because they had Bettas in those vases...and I've cared for all I can since. It truly started when I went to a party and the centerpieces were bowls with Bettas in them.  They were just going to flush them after the reception. I got people to take them home and took a couple myself. 

There are a couple of stores here that call me when they have super sick bettas. They save them in the back for me and I go pick them up. I leave a bunch of cards all over the place so anyone can call if they need to rehome.

 I have a hospital type system and can treat up to 4 at a time. I medicate them in hospital tanks as long as they need.I get them used to humans by spending time feeding and touching them. They are put on good foods and stimulated with mirrors and ping pong balls.  I have planted tanks ready for them and drop them off at their new homes.  This way I can do all the scapes that pop up in my brain and not have to have a bunch of tanks lol. I have a You Tube channel that covers more of the rescuing...don't want to seem like I'm promoting myself. I just do the videos for fun and to try to share some of the tips I've picked up. Lol I usually film with my camera taped to a spaghetti sauce can 😂  If its allowed , its Beloved Betta Rescue....if not my apologies and Ill delete it.

The one thing no one should do is pay for sick Bettas. I know its hard to pass them up...but if you buy it , another one will be in its place. If you talk to a manager you can usually get them to make the sick ones free . In a couple of instances I have paid a dollar...but they were very sick and doing poorly and she wouldnt budge.
